title: Visual mode
goal: Select exactly the text you mean - by character, line or column - and apply any operator to it.

lessons.title: Charwise and linewise selections

concepts.desc: start a charwise / linewise selection. Any motion extends it.
delete / change / yank the selection.
jump to the other end of the selection, to extend it the other way.
reselect the last visual selection.
replace the selection with the register contents.
leave visual mode without doing anything.

lessons.tip: Visual mode is great when you need to see what you're about to change. But if a plain operator + motion works (d3j, cE), it's shorter and . can repeat it.

quiz.q: Which key selects whole lines?
You selected too little at the top of a selection. How do you move the start of the selection instead of the end?
How do you reselect what you last had selected?
What does `p` do while text is selected?
quiz.a: Replaces the selection with the register contents (the replaced text goes into the unnamed register).

quiz.q: Select the current line plus the two below and delete them, using visual mode.
Why is `d2j` often better than `Vjjd`?
quiz.a: Fewer keys, and . can repeat it exactly.

lessons.title: Visual block: editing columns

concepts.desc: start a rectangular (block) selection.
in block mode: insert text before the block on every line.
in block mode: append text at the end of every line, even when the lines have different lengths.
change / replace every char / delete the whole column.
in block mode: jump to the other corner on the same line.

lessons.tip: The block edit only shows on the first line while you type; the other lines update when you press Esc. That's normal.

quiz.q: Prefix 10 lines with `// ` using visual block mode.
Lines have different lengths. How do you append `;` to all of them with block mode?
You typed in block-insert mode but only the first line changed. What do you do?
quiz.a: Press Esc; the change is copied to the other lines then.

quiz.q: What does `r-` do on a block selection?
Which key starts block selection?
In block mode, what's the difference between o and O?
quiz.a: o goes to the diagonally opposite corner; O goes to the other corner on the same line.

lessons.title: Case, joining and indenting selections

concepts.desc: in visual: lowercase / uppercase / toggle case of the selection.
join the selected lines (gJ adds no spaces).
indent / unindent the selected lines by shiftwidth. Use a count (3>) for more levels.
auto-indent the selection (uses the filetype's indent rules).
after a visual operation, . repeats it on the same amount of text from the cursor.

lessons.tip: In visual mode u lowercases, it does NOT undo. If you mean undo, press Esc first.

quiz.q: What does `u` do in visual mode?
Uppercase the current word using visual mode.
quiz.a: viwU (or veU from the word start)

quiz.q: Indent the selected lines two levels at once.
Join 4 selected lines without adding spaces between them.
Which key re-indents a selected block of code according to the filetype?
You pressed > on a selection and want to do it again on the same lines.

lessons.title: Selecting with text objects

concepts.desc: select inner word / word plus trailing space.
select inside brackets or quotes (va... includes the delimiters).
select the paragraph / paragraph plus the blank line after it.
pressing ip, i( etc. again grows the selection to the next level.
select inside / around an XML or HTML tag.

lessons.tip: Use v + text object to check what an object covers before you use it with an operator: vi( shows what di( would delete.

quiz.q: Select a whole function body separated by blank lines, including the trailing blank line.
Select the text inside double quotes, without the quotes.
You did vi( and want to grow the selection to the enclosing parens' contents. What do you press?
quiz.a: i( again (or a( to include the parens).

quiz.q: Difference between vi{ and va{?
quiz.a: vi{ selects inside the braces; va{ includes the braces.

quiz.q: Select the content of an HTML tag.
Why practice v + text object before d + text object?
quiz.a: You see exactly what the object covers before you change anything.

lessons.title: Week 5 review

concepts.desc: the three selection modes
adjust or reselect
block edits
selection operators
text-object selections

lessons.tip: Ask yourself each time: would a plain operator + motion be shorter? Use visual mode when you need to see the selection, or for columns.

quiz.q: Comment out 5 lines with `# ` using block mode.
Uppercase the whole current line using visual mode.
Reselect the last selection and indent it.
Select the paragraph the cursor is in, without the blank line after it.
Replace a selected word with the text you yanked earlier.
Append ` \` to the end of 6 lines of different lengths.
